name: Cool Green
lede: Cool Green is a vivid, blue-leaning modifier on [[green]], first recorded in the 2010 xkcd color survey, where thousands of internet users typed their own name for the hue they were shown.

sections.title: A crowd-sourced modifier
sections.body:
The name follows the library's plain modifier grammar: *cool* plus [[green]], marking it as the blue-leaning side of the green family rather than a historical or commercial name [1]. Its only record is the xkcd color survey of 2010, an open web poll with no earlier dictionary or standard behind it, so no coiner or date beyond that survey is documented [1]. Our library also groups it with [[emerald]] as a related name [1].

Its nearest named neighbors are [[algae-green]], almost indistinguishable at 3.1 units, and [[shamrock]] and [[jade-green]], both a touch more vivid or duller at 3.6 [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive carries a color this close to Cool Green covering at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [3]. That says more about this particular archive of old paintings than about green paint in general: a crowd-sourced web name like this one was never meant to describe historical pigments [3].

origin.named_after: a modifier on green; coined by a respondent to the 2010 xkcd color survey

questions.q: Where does the name Cool Green come from?
True or false: Cool Green covers at least one percent of the canvas in several paintings in our archive.

openers: Cool Green comes from a 2010 internet survey, not a dictionary or a pigment.
